objective: Verify that a sub-three-minute competition video can explain concrete accepted inputs, concrete outputs, the typical manual baseline and observable efficiency mechanisms while retaining six real-product operation chapters.

iterations.finding: The detailed first draft would exceed the 180-second competition limit.
iterations.resolution: Kept complete details on the slide and operation rail, shortened spoken repetition and raised narration rate from +18% to +28%.

iterations.finding: The measurement rail remained visible while the source recording had already changed to the delivery page.
iterations.resolution: Separated the source-video boundaries for measurement and delivery.

iterations.finding: The first boundary correction froze a blank transition frame at the end of the measurement narration.
iterations.resolution: Inspected raw frames from 57.5 to 59.0 seconds and fixed the measurement endpoint at the stable 58.0-second designed result; delivery begins at 61.5 seconds.

iterations.finding: Ten slides, six operation chapters and timed subtitles remain legible; representative frames show the concrete input/output and stable successful operation state.

evidenceBoundary: The result proves the technical workflow, visible workflow changes and a reproducible presentation artifact. It does not prove a fixed productivity percentage, long-term deployment outcome or official competition score.
